source.title: How do you feel--now? The anterior insula and human awareness

confidence_rationale: The canonical statement that the anterior insula re-represents interoceptive state and that this re-representation is the basis of subjective feelings -- the biological seat of the E1-representable satisfaction/affective state MECH-214 requires. Strong source, but mapping fidelity is moderate: Craig describes WHERE and THAT interoception is re-represented, not the REE-specific failure mode (wanting fires on an E1-unrepresented satisfaction state). Held at 0.60.
failure_signatures: If the satisfaction/homeostatic state a goal aims at is not re-represented in an interoceptive self-channel, there is no felt-feeling against which attainment can be registered -- the MECH-214 wanting-without-grounding failure: pursuit of a proxy whose hedonic/satisfaction referent is never E1-represented.

Subjective feelings depend on AIC re-representation of body state; a self-model with only exteroceptive z_self (body schema, no interoceptive channel) would predict action capacity yet have no representable satisfaction state -- the MECH-215 capacity-vs-affect gap.

The AIC's involvement spans craving, homeostatic drives, and decision -- so an agent lacking this channel could pursue goals without the affective evaluation that distinguishes wanting from liking (the addiction-mapping prediction).

mapping.source_claim_statement: The anterior insular cortex re-represents interoceptive state (the physiological condition of the body) and this re-representation provides a basis for all subjective feelings and for awareness; it is implicated across homeostatic drives, craving, emotion, and decision-making.
mapping.ree_translation: Craig's interoceptive re-representation is the biological seat of the E1-representable satisfaction/affective self-state MECH-214 requires: a goal's satisfaction referent must be representable in E1's schema space (here, an interoceptive self-channel) for z_goal to carry semantic hedonic information. Without it, wanting fires on an E1-unrepresented state -- the addiction/anhedonia mapping. The interoceptive self-state is also the affective half of MECH-215's z_self subject.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A review of insula function in humans, not a test of the REE failure mode. It grounds the EXISTENCE and locus of an interoceptive self-representation (so the MECH-214 channel is biologically real) but says nothing about REE's z_goal/z_self wiring or whether an agent lacking the channel shows the predicted wanting-without-satisfaction pathology -- that remains the V4 DR-14 experiment. The anterior insula is harvested as a completion-set partner (interoceptive-self locus), proposal-first.
mapping.source_context: Human functional neuroanatomy review; anterior insular cortex, von Economo neurons, interoception and awareness.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high (Nat Rev Neurosci, the canonical interoception-awareness review). Mapping fidelity moderate: establishes that an interoceptive self-representation exists and where, but the MECH-214 failure mode (wanting on an unrepresented satisfaction state) is REE-specific and untested here. Transfer risk moderate -- human neuroanatomy to a REE interoceptive-goal channel that V3 does not yet have.
